title: Chapter 223: He Has to Be a Patient!
html:
“What’s wrong?” The sight of Xiao Du drenched in cold sweat made Su Luoluo nervous as well.

“I’ll tell you, but don’t panic.” Xiao Du huddled close to her. “I think this place might actually be haunted.”

“Don’t try to scare me.” Su Luoluo had visited many Haunted Houses, but she had never encountered one like Boss Chen’s. It was a maze that visitors could explore without restriction.

“Everything Mr. Han guessed was wrong. Not a single worker was hiding among those mannequins—they moved by themselves!” Xiao Du clenched his hands until his knuckles cracked. “We can’t rely on Mr. Han. I have to tell Boss and Brother Song.”

“They left ages ago... Wait, don’t run so fast!” Xiao Du bolted ahead, leaving Su Luoluo behind. She could not decide whether to chase him or remain with Ye Xiaoxin and wait for Mr. Han.

“A Haunted House that’s truly haunted? Mannequins moving by themselves?” Ye Xiaoxin recorded both observations in her notebook. “It can even frighten professional actors from another Haunted House. This place really is something else.”

Her assessment was glowing. “It’s been a long time since I encountered a Haunted House of this quality. Today should be fun.”

“The boy didn’t look as though he was lying,” Su Luoluo reminded her. “We should keep moving too. It’s safer to stay together.”

“In my opinion, Haunted Houses are no different from magic. Both rely on illusion and psychological misdirection to surprise their audiences. The more convincing the illusion, the greater the success.” Ye Xiaoxin removed her jacket and tied it around her waist. She stretched lazily, her voluptuous figure making her sole audience a little uncomfortable. “By that measure, Western Jiujiang’s House of Horrors is undeniably successful.”

“Then you can stay here. I’m going to catch up with them.”

The visitors split up. None of them noticed the bloody writing on the walls growing darker, as though the blood were trying to seep free.

…

“Boss, stop defending him. Han Qiuming may be talented, but that doesn’t mean we should let him insult us!” Song An was furious on Guo Miao’s behalf. “Yes, he created the design, but all of us helped build the set. He barely took part in the construction, so what gives him the right to be so proud?”

“Calm down. I understand everything you’re saying, but a little patience goes a long way. He is the designer our sponsor invited, after all.” Guo Miao was old enough to let many things go. “Haunted Houses are a dying trade, and all of us are simply trying to make a living. There’s no reason to turn on one another.”

“Didn’t you see how arrogant he was? He even wants to replace you! Honestly, if the sponsor listens to him and removes you as Boss, I’ll resign on the spot.” Song An had always been forthright.

“Don’t worry. The sponsor won’t agree.” Guo Miao sighed, though in truth, he was far from confident. Their attendance had been declining ever since they were forced to leave Xing Hai. “Let’s find the tape recorder first. Fans of Tian Teng Medical School are waiting outside; we can’t disappoint them.”

“Okay.” The two continued onward. They turned a corner only to find themselves in yet another corridor. “What is this supposed to be? Do they expect us to keep walking forever?”

The corridor was dim, its walls darkening like bruised flesh. As they stepped over the uneven mattresses, breathing air permeated by antibiotics and a strange stench, they felt as if they were crawling through the intestines of some monstrous creature.

“Boss Chen must have had a reason for designing it this way. He probably wanted it to feel more authentic.” Guo Miao peeled a fragment from the wall, and it crumbled between his fingers. “Along the way, I noticed that some of the room numbers had been left intact. Every room in the first corridor began with a four, those in the second began with a three, and the ones here begin with two.”

“The numbers are decreasing?”

“I suspect this entire scenario is based on a four-story building, and Boss Chen has reproduced it exactly. Each corridor represents a different floor.” Guo Miao studied the walls. “Even the room numbers retain their age and wear. Not a single detail has been overlooked. This goes far beyond ordinary perfectionism.”

“I had the same impression. We build Haunted Houses primarily to scare visitors, but Boss Chen seems intent on reconstructing something. The sheer amount of detail—even the bloody messages on the walls—borders on obsession.” As Song An’s anger faded, fear took its place. “The messages haven’t stopped since we entered. It’s hard to imagine how he managed to write all of them.”

“Some look fresher than others.” Guo Miao felt uneasy too. An image formed in his mind: the Haunted House’s owner alone in the dark at midnight, carrying a bucket of red paint and scrawling message after message like a man possessed.

“Before we entered, Boss Chen said the Haunted House had been operating for five or six years. Could he have planned this scenario with his parents?”

“Why spend five years building a single scenario?” As someone in the same business, Guo Miao knew how much time and effort a scenario this elaborate required. “At the entrance, some of us peeled back the flooring. Boss Chen even paid attention to places ordinary visitors would never examine. That level of detail is deeply unnatural.”

“Wait—the name ‘Third Sick Hall’ sounds familiar now.” Song An pulled out his phone, and his expression fell when he saw the search results. “Boss, the Third Sick Hall was a real place in Jiujiang! Its patients were involved in several crimes, including murder. The police even issued a warrant for escaped patients a few days ago!”

“So Boss Chen wasn’t lying?” Guo Miao’s pupils contracted. “He glossed over something that important?”

“According to the internet, the Third Sick Hall was abandoned five years ago—and his Haunted House opened five years ago!” Song An compared the timelines. They matched.

“This is bad!” Guo Miao suddenly remembered something. “Read those articles carefully. Check the wanted notice and see whether anyone matches Boss Chen—height, weight, anything.”

“Boss, do you think Boss Chen was once a patient at the Third Sick Hall?”

“Would a normal person spend five years reconstructing a mental hospital? Every detail here is authentic. Only someone who had lived in a mental hospital for a long time could reproduce it this perfectly!” The longer Guo Miao considered it, the more frightened he became. “Boss Chen cleared Tian Teng Medical School without his heart rate exceeding one hundred even once. How could someone like that possibly be normal?”

“How about we just stop this tour and leave immediately?”

“Leaving now might cause us to get targeted.”

“Why?”

“The Third Sick Hall isn’t normally open to visitors, and Boss Chen claimed the scenario was unfinished. Looking back, those were probably excuses.” Guo Miao wanted to strangle Han Qiuming. “This place must be hiding an enormous secret.”

Seeing the gravity of Guo Miao’s expression, Song An lowered his voice. “What kind of secret?”

“Before coming here, I spoke with New Century Park’s manager. He happened to mention that Boss Chen’s parents vanished without a trace half a year ago.” Guo Miao stared at the deranged sentences written in blood, his heart frozen with fear.

“They vanished?” Song An’s shock gave way to terror. His eyes widened as though something had suddenly occurred to him.
